Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM Center, EDSA corner Quezon Avenue, west Triangle, Quezon City http: //www.dilg.com.ph OILG OPINION NO. DR. WALTER RANDOLPH C. JALGALADO Sanggunian Panlalawigan Member ISt District Province of Camarines Norte Pl Barangay Binanuan, Talisay, Camarines Norte Dear Dr. Jalgalado: This has reference to the letter you sent dated 25 September 2019, seeking this Department's clarification and legal opinion on the exercise of local legislative power so the members of the SP may be enlightened: In the said letter, a brief background of the facts are as follows: • Pursuant to Sec. 28, Article 2 of the 1987 Constitution of the Philippines which provides that subject to reasonable conditions set by law, the State adopts and implements a policy of full public disclosure of all its transactions involving public interest and the passage of Executive Order (EO) No. 2, entitled "Operationalizing in the Executive Branch the People's Right to Information and the State Policies to Full Public Disclosure and Transparency in the Public Service and Providing for Guidelines, thereof", Dr. Walter Randolph C. Jalgalado, Hon. Arthur Michael Canlas, and Hon. Godfrey Parale, Board Members of Camarines Norte, submitted Draft Resolution No. 063-2019 or the Camarines Norte Freedom of Information Ordinance of 2019 (FOI Ordinance) for the consideration of the SP. The measure was referred to the Committee on Good Government, who in turn, referred the same to the Office of the Provincial Legal officer for his evaluation. The Provincial Legal Officer, Atty. Doon Culvera, in his legal opinion purports that the SP must not enact the proposed ordinance so that it will not encroach upon the sole prerogative of the Congress to legislate for the reason that the proposed ordinance cites Sec. 28, Art. 2 of the Constitution as its rationale for the proposed course of action and the Congress has not yet enacted a law prescribing the conditions for the realization of such policy. Also, Atty. Culvera opined that the enactment of the proposed ordinance is no longer necessary to implement the desired policy because EO No. 2 already serves that purpose.

• • The SP was also made aware of the Joint Memorandum Circular 2018- 01 of this Department and the Presidential Communications Operations Office entitled Reiteration of EO No. 2 s 2016 "Operationalizing in the Executive Branch the People's Right to Information and the State Policies to Full Public Disclosure and Transparency in the Public Service". However, the proposed FOI Ordinance was not passed and was subsequently recommended as Laid on the Table. Under this premise arose the request for clarification and legal opinion on the exercise of local legislative power so the members of the SP may be enlightened as to the issue on encroachment of the legislative prerogative that has been reserved by the Constitution only in the Congress. At the outset, it is true that local government units (LGUs) exercise only delegated legislative powers conferred by Congress, but we must also recognize that the Constitutionl itself guarantees autonomy to LGUs. Accordingly, the Local Government Code of 1991 (LGC) was enacted as the grant of the authority to prescribe local regulations. This delegation is based on the principle that the local government is in better position than the national government to act on purely local concerns. Legislative power is therefore given to them for effective local legislation. In view thereof, it is imperative to cite herein the pertinent provisions of the LGC, as amended, in relation to local legislative power: "Section 48. Local Legislative Power. - Local legislative power shall be exercised by the sangguniang panlalawigan for the province; the sangguniang panlungsod for the city; the sangguniang bayan for the municipality; and the sangguniang barangay for the barangay. xxx xxx xxx Section 458. Powers, Duties, Functions and Compensation. (a) The sangguniang panlungsod, as the legislative body of the city, shall enact ordinances, approve resolutions and appropriate funds for the general welfare of the city and its inhabitants pursuant to Section 16 of this Code and in the proper exercise of the corporate powers of the city as provided for under Section 22 of this Code, and shall: (I) Approve ordinances and pass resolutions necessary for an efficient and effective city government, and in this connection, shall: 1 Sec. 2, Art. X. The 1987 Philippine Constitution.

xxx xxx xxx We now delve on the issue on whether the enactment of the proposed ordinance would encroach on the prerogative Of the Congress to legislate, for the reason that there is no enabling law in connection with the State policy in which the proposed ordinance is Sec. 28, Art. 2 of the Constitution, which reads: "SECTION 28. Subject to reasonable conditions prescribed by law, the State adopts and implements a policy of full public disclosure of all its transactions involving public interest. " This Department is of the view that the proposed ordinance does not encroach upon the law-making power vested in the Congress. Notwithstanding that statements and principles of policies are generally not self-executing, a constitutional provision is considered self-executing when it can be given effect without the aid of legislation, and there is nothing to indicate that legislation is intended to make it operative. As a matter of fact, Section 2 of the said E.O. encourages the LGUs to observe the order and be guided thereby. Accordingly, E.O. No. 2 is the enabling order for FOI. EO No.2 operationalizes in the Executive Branch the people's constitutional right to information and it also provides the State policies to full public disclosure and transparency in the public service. The policy on full public disclosure is reiterated in the Bill of Rights, particularly, Sec. 7, Article 3 of the Constitution, to wit: "SECTION 7. The right of the people to information on matters of public concern shall be recognized. Access to official records, and to documents, and papers pertaining to official acts, transactions, or decisions, as well as to government research data used as basis for policy development, shall be afforded the citizen, subject to such limitations as may be provided by law. " Likewise, it is important to note that the proposed ordinance takes into account the conditions and/or limitations set forth in RA 10173 (The Data-Privacy Act of 2012) on the policy of full public disclosure, which is an existing law. Further, Sections 3 (h) and (m) and Section 16 of the LGC provide that there shall be a continuing mechanism to enhance local autonomy not only by legislative enabling acts but also by administrative and organizational reforms, that the national government shall ensure that decentralization contributes to the continuing improvement of the performance of LGUs and the quality of community life, that each LGU shall exercise its powers essential to the promotion of the general welfare and provision of basic services and facilities. Moreover, pursuant to the issuance of E.O. No. 2, by the President, and the mandate of this Department to assist the President in the exercise of general

supervision over local governments in the promulgation of policies, rules, regulations and other issuances on general supervision over local governments and on public order and safety, this Department and the Presidential Communications Office issued a Joint Memorandum Circular (DILG-PCOO JMC 2018-012) which seeks to reiterate E.O. No. 2, thereby encouraging the provinces, cities, and municipalities to enact an ordinance, or issue a local chief executive's Order, in support of FOI. We hope to have addressed your concern accordingly. Thank you. Very truly yours, BY AUTHORITY OF THE SECRETARY MARIVEL Unders COPY FURNISHED: ATTY. ANTHONY C. NUYDA, CESO 111 REGIONAL DIRECTOR DILG-REGION 5 Rizal St., Legazpi City LLLS/ 2 .
